questions.q: Name the two main sub-categories of non-clastic sedimentary rocks and give one characteristic example of each.
questions.a: Chemically formed (e.g., limestone, rock salt, gypsum) and organically formed (e.g., coal, chalk, coquina). A wrong answer that lists sandstone or shale reveals confusion with mechanically formed (clastic) rocks covered in the previous node.

questions.q: Explain why limestone can be classified as both a chemically formed and an organically formed sedimentary rock.
questions.a: Limestone (CaCO₃) precipitates chemically from calcium-rich water in caves (stalactites) or shallow seas (ooids) — chemical origin. It also forms from the accumulation of shells, coral, and foraminifera tests — organic origin. A student who says "limestone is only chemical" misses the dual genesis and the concept of biogenic precipitation.

questions.q: A coal sample from the Jharia coalfield shows distinct bright and dull bands. Identify the maceral groups responsible and state what each indicates about the original plant material and depositional conditions.
questions.a: Bright bands = vitrinite (woody tissue, humid conditions); dull bands = inertinite (oxidized/charred material, drier/fire-prone) or liptinite (spores/resins, anoxic). Correct interpretation requires linking macerals to plant parts and palaeoenvironment. A wrong answer (e.g., "bands are impurities") shows ignorance of coal petrology basics.

questions.q: Compare the depositional environments of the Vindhyan limestone (Central India) and the Gondwana coal seams (Damodar Valley). What tectonic-climatic setting does each imply?
questions.a: Vindhyan limestone: stable shallow marine shelf (Proterozoic), warm clear water, low clastic input → chemical/biogenic precipitation. Gondwana coal: fluvial-deltaic basins in rift valleys (Permian), temperate glacial-to-warm climate, high plant productivity, rapid burial. A student who places both in "water" without distinguishing marine vs. terrestrial fluvial systems fails to analyse tectonic control.

questions.q: Evaluate the statement: "All limestone deposits in India are suitable for cement manufacturing." Justify with reference to mineral purity and stratigraphic age.
questions.a: False. Cement-grade limestone requires >90% CaCO₃ and low MgO, SiO₂, Al₂O₃. Many Indian limestones (e.g., some Vindhyan, Cuddapah) are argillaceous or dolomitic. Only specific horizons (e.g., parts of Bilaspur, Kurnool, Jaisalmer) meet specs. A "True" answer ignores geochemical variability and industrial specifications.

questions.q: Design a field observation checklist for a Class 11 student visiting a limestone quarry and a coal mine to distinguish their formation processes. Include 4 diagnostic features for each rock type.
questions.a: Limestone checklist: (1) reaction with dilute HCl, (2) fossil shells/corals, (3) bedding planes with stylolites, (4) cave/karts features nearby. Coal checklist: (1) black streak, (2) conchoidal fracture, (3) plant impressions (bark, leaves), (4) association with sandstone/shale cyclothems. A poor checklist lists only colour or hardness, missing process-specific evidence.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Chemically formed sedimentary rocks (e.g., limestone, rock salt, gypsum) precipitate from dissolved minerals in water through evaporation or chemical reactions, while organically formed sedimentary rocks (e.g., coal, chalk, some limestones) originate from the accumulation and ______ of plant or animal remains.

Fill in the blank: Observe a piece of limestone from a local building or a coal sample from a nearby thermal power plant; notice the fine layering in limestone and the black, lightweight, ______ appearance of coal.
What is Chemically formed sedimentary rocks (e? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Chemically formed sedimentary rocks (e.g., limestone, rock salt, gypsum) precipitate from dissolved minerals in water through evaporation or chemical reactions, while organically formed sedimentary rocks (e.g., coal, chalk, some limestones) originate from the accumulation and lithification of plant or animal remains.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Connect to the rock cycle (node ______) where sedimentary rocks form from pre-existing material.
What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Chemically formed sedimentary rocks (e?
questions.a: Students think "organic rocks contain organic matter" — they believe coal is made of undecomposed plant material.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: Student can distinguish between chemically and organically formed sedimentary rocks by their origin, composition, and texture; explain the formation processes of limestone (both chemical and organic) and coal with correct geological terminology; and identify their typical Indian occurrences on a map.
